headline: India says it does not endorse Sheikh Hasina's remarks at New Delhi event
summary: The Indian government distanced itself from a media interaction involving the deposed Bangladeshi PM, calling it a private event.
details: The Indian Ministry of External Affairs stated that it does not endorse any remarks made by deposed Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and other Awami League leaders during a media event in New Delhi on August 5.
Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified that the event was hosted by the Foreign Correspondents’ Club of South Asia, a private media entity, and the Indian government had no role in its organization.

During the event, Hasina reiterated her intention to return to Bangladesh in December this year. She has been sheltered in India since fleeing the country on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising.
Bangladesh's foreign ministry issued a strong statement, calling the interaction an "affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh" and a "grievous insult to the martyrs of the July Revolution."
The Bangladesh government has previously sent letters to India seeking Hasina's extradition, though no response has yet been received.
Prime Minister’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir had urged New Delhi to ensure that Indian territory is not used for political statements aimed at creating instability in Bangladesh.
BNP and National Citizen Party leaders also criticized the Indian government, alleging that Hasina is being used as a tool to destabilize the country.

Bilateral relations between Bangladesh and India have remained strained since the ouster of the Awami League government, despite some signs of improvement following the formation of the BNP government in February.

headline: Govt says no way for Shakib to return after event with Sheikh Hasina
summary: Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque states there is no longer any room for flexibility after the cricketer's virtual appearance alongside the ousted prime minister.
details: Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque announced that former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan has no prospect of returning to play after joining a media event with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
The minister stated that while the government had previously been flexible and tolerant, his appearance alongside the 'autocrat' has changed the situation and removed any opportunity for his return.
Shakib, 39, joined the New Delhi event virtually on Wednesday, where he called for peace and progress in Bangladesh, stating he has no regrets about his appearance.

The cricketer told Reuters that he is ready to return to Bangladesh from his two-year exile, face trial on charges including murder, and play a farewell series if the government guarantees his safety.
Shakib has been living in the US since August 2024 and faces two active cases: one regarding the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another involving alleged corruption.

caption:
No more flexibility. The government has shut the door on Shakib Al Hasan's return to Bangladesh.

Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque announced that former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan has no prospect of returning to play after joining a media event with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

The minister stated that while the government had previously been flexible and tolerant, his appearance alongside the 'autocrat' has changed the situation and removed any opportunity for his return.

Shakib, 39, joined the New Delhi event virtually on Wednesday, where he called for peace and progress in Bangladesh, stating he has no regrets about his appearance.

The cricketer told Reuters that he is ready to return to Bangladesh from his two-year exile, face trial on charges including murder, and play a farewell series if the government guarantees his safety.

Shakib has been living in the US since August 2024 and faces two active cases: one regarding the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another involving alleged corruption.

He also revealed that his bank accounts have been frozen for a year and a half and that he not yet seen his parents, who remain in Bangladesh and have not been allowed to leave.
